topic: What creates the Earth's magnetic field (and why does it move)?

primary_direction.name: GEODYNAMO-X
primary_direction.claim: A coupled physical state-space model with explicit core, induced, ionospheric, and magnetospheric sources can improve calibrated held-out prediction and source attribution of geomagnetic variation over static, core-only, and uncoupled baselines.
primary_direction.research_object: A latent-state model of outer-core magnetic dynamics, core-mantle-boundary flow, conducting transfer layers, and external current systems assimilated from ground, satellite, and paleomagnetic observations.
primary_direction.falsification: Reject the direction if the coupled model fails synthetic-twin state recovery or does not improve held-out vector-field and secular-variation skill under equal data, forecast windows, and parameter-budget accounting.

candidate_routes.name: uncoupled source separation
candidate_routes.weakness: cannot express shared dynamics or feedback

candidate_routes.name: GEODYNAMO-X
candidate_routes.strength: joint dynamics, source separation, identifiability, and forecast evaluation

predictions: Joint assimilation improves held-out vector-field and secular-variation prediction.
External-source states reduce false attribution of geomagnetic storms to core acceleration.
Physical priors improve forecast extrapolation more than in-sample fit.
Synthetic twins expose which core-flow scales and buoyancy parameters are identifiable.
